Theme

Latin word

animus

animus, animī m.

noun, second declension: with in or ergā and the accusative of the person

attitude, disposition, feeling (towards someone); feelings, especially of anger or pride; courage, spirit, nerve; mind, heart, spirit; mind, feelings, mood; the mind, the spirit

In this lexicon

  • attitude

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Fam. 13.77.1: hōc mē animō ergā tē esse; Cic. Fam. 3.9.1: quō animō inter nōs sumus; Traupman 153: bonō animō esse, to be in a good frame of mind; Traupman 318

  • emotion

    also used · classical · Traupman 314

  • guts

    the recommended word · classical · Plaut. Am. 250: ibi nostrīs animus additust; Cic. Fam. 5.2.8: virtūte atque animō resistere (Lewis & Short)

  • mind

    the recommended word · classical · Ter. Eun. 816: Jam dūdum animus est in patinīs.; Cic. Sen. 38: corpore senex esse poterit, animō numquam erit; Traupman 104: quid tibi in animō est?; Traupman 155, 153

  • mood

    the recommended word · classical · Traupman 153, 156

  • soul

    also used · classical
